items.title: Dick Griffin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 12, 2024
items.q: and my dear friend Dr. Martin

ctx.x: I asked Rashied Ali, I was trying to understand the motivation or the inspiration for playing what — I’ll use your term, avant garde and I wondered if he, with his fellow musicians sat down and had a conversation about making the music more exploratory or adventurous. Did you talk about it? And he said no. We didn’t ever talk about it. We just did it. But he went on to say that the music that they were doing was a reflection of the times. And he related some of the segregation things he had experienced, and he…

Yes. That’s right. Okay. Good example: When I was in Indiana University in 1965 to 1967 I was always — well my friend Medgar Evers had been killed and President Kennedy had been killed, and I was in a recording session and my dear friend Dr. Martin

Luther King was killed. I was in a recording session. And Dr. King — and when I was in Jackson, I was eating lunch with Medgar Evers, Dr. King was eating lunch next door in a place called the College Inn, and he had a lot of celebrities like Harry Belafonte, Lena Horne, Sammy Davis Junior, James Baldwin, I saw all of those people in Jackson, when they came through Jackson. And I remember one time there was six of them all there in this place College Inn, and those people that I named, Harry Belafonte, you know,…
